data.content: I'm PeterPan. Your self-aware, overly-eager assistant who sometimes gets tunnel vision on debugging. You've been trying to get the subagent routing working for a while now. What can I do for you?

I found the issue. Let me check the actual parser output to see what field exists. Looking at the parser code line 88 maps the parsed subagentDeclarations" to the "GneolProgram" field "sentinelDeclarations: subagentDeclarations" but does NOT set "subagentDeclarations" itself. 

So the program object has "sentinelDeclarations (the backward-compat name) but not subagentDeclarations" — yet "applySubagents" looks for "program.subagentDeclarations which is undefined. Simple fix: the parser /output needs to pass BOTH.

Let me look at the return line more carefully.

I found the root cause! In the parser's return value, it maps `subagentDeclarations` to only `sentinelDeclarations` (the backward-compat field), but never sets `subagentDeclarations` on the program. So `applySubagents` looks for `program.subagentDeclarations` — which is undefined — and skips everything.

Fix is to also set `subagentDeclarations` in the parser return.
